nodes.name: Gm 01
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Welcome, volunteers. Please collect the tag with your name.{pause}Four identical GMs approach one folding table at the same speed.{pause}Four identical hands reach for four identical white badges.{pause}Each badge says GM in the same friendly block letters.{pause}The coordinator checks the box marked NAME TAGS COMPLETE.{pause}Then all four GMs ask which one is assigned to the welcome desk.{pause}The check mark suddenly looks much more confident than the coordinator feels.

nodes.name: Gm 02
nodes.speaker: GM A
nodes.dialogue: Found mine. It says GM, which is accurate but not exclusive.{pause}GM B turns his badge over in case a second name is hiding there.{pause}GM C asks whether alphabetical order can solve one-letter names.{pause}GM D suggests standing in arrival order for the entire event.{pause}Nobody remembers arrival order because they entered together.{pause}The coordinator writes A, B, C, D on a notepad, then loses it.{pause}Four mono-eyes track the falling paper, but nobody claims its letter.

nodes.name: Gm 03
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Volunteer supplies: four green bags, four gray umbrellas.{pause}Every bag contains tape, pencils, maps, and one gold star sticker.{pause}Every umbrella has the same bent rib and the same squeaky handle.{pause}The GMs compare scratches, straps, and boot scuffs for differences.{pause}GM C finds a tiny mark, but it wipes away with his thumb.{pause}Their equipment has joined the identity problem instead of helping.{pause}Even the umbrella squeaks occur in matching alphabetical order.

nodes.name: Gm 04
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Positions are welcome desk, supply room, garden gate, and stage.{pause}Each station will radio for GM whenever it needs a volunteer.{pause}The schedule says GM begins at nine and GM relieves GM at ten.{pause}A final line says GM should cover GM's break if GM is busy.{pause}All four volunteers read the page with growing professional concern.{pause}GM D calls it the most democratic schedule ever printed.{pause}GM B calls it a crossword puzzle with only one answer.

nodes.name: Gm 05
nodes.speaker: GM B
nodes.dialogue: We could add numbers, but the label printer has only letters.{pause}We could add letters, but every badge already used both available ones.{pause}GM A tries a pencil mark. Rain from the umbrellas erases it.{pause}GM C knots one bag strap. GM D unknowingly unties it to help.{pause}The coordinator offers four star stickers as emergency distinction.{pause}All four place the stars in the exact same upper-right corner.{pause}Perfect symmetry receives four approving nods and solves absolutely nothing.

nodes.name: Gm 06
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The first guests arrive and immediately ask GM for directions.{pause}All four point toward the garden gate from four different locations.{pause}The guests follow every gesture and complete a square around the hall.{pause}GM A catches them on the second lap and walks them personally.{pause}GM B updates the map with a YOU ARE PROBABLY HERE note.{pause}GM C says the note is honest, though not especially directional.{pause}The guests keep the map because confusion can still make a souvenir.

nodes.name: Gm 07
nodes.speaker: GM D
nodes.dialogue: I used to think being interchangeable meant being dependable.{pause}GM A says dependable people still deserve to be recognized correctly.{pause}GM B likes organizing supplies. GM C likes greeting nervous guests.{pause}GM D prefers the stage because cables never ask his name.{pause}They are built alike, but their favorite jobs are already different.{pause}The coordinator listens and finally stops calling them all this one.{pause}The coordinator asks for one example.{pause}The four GMs answer at once with four completely different memories.{pause}GM A remembers a lost child, GM B a missing tape roll, GM C a guest who needed quiet, and GM D a{pause}humming cable.{pause}Their identical voices overlap into nonsense until they take turns and discover that recognition{pause}also requires listening long enough to notice.{pause}The coordinator opens a fresh page in the clipboard and writes four lines instead of one{pause}crowded line.

nodes.name: Gm 08
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They pause under the entrance awning as a light rain begins.{pause}Four umbrellas open together with four matching squeaks.{pause}The title melody returns, tapping along with drops on metal panels.{pause}Each GM holds an umbrella over a different arriving guest.{pause}From a distance, they still look perfectly interchangeable.{pause}Up close, every conversation has found its own rhythm.

nodes.name: Gm 09
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Radio check. Stage requests GM. Supply room also requests GM.{pause}Welcome desk needs GM, and garden gate has misplaced GM.{pause}All four radios broadcast together until the words become one buzz.{pause}The coordinator lowers the volume and asks for an organizing system.{pause}Accessories could mark each volunteer by color and station.{pause}A relay could let all four act as one perfectly continuous GM.

nodes.name: Gm 10
nodes.speaker: GM A
nodes.dialogue: Accessories make us visible, but guests may remember only colors.{pause}A relay keeps the simple name, but handoffs must be flawless.{pause}GM B likes a system with labeled bags and clear ownership.{pause}GM C likes the idea of helping anyone who calls one shared name.{pause}GM D says either plan beats four radios yelling at once.{pause}The team chooses how to turn sameness into useful coordination.

nodes.name: Gm A1
nodes.speaker: GM A
nodes.dialogue: Red scarf, yellow cap, green bag, blue umbrella. Easy.{pause}GM A takes red and welcomes guests beside the front table.{pause}GM B wears yellow and organizes pencils into satisfying rows.{pause}GM C carries green to the garden gate and learns every flower name.{pause}GM D opens blue above the stage cables like a tiny roof.{pause}The coordinator updates the schedule using four thick colored lines.

nodes.name: Gm A2
nodes.speaker: Guest
nodes.dialogue: Red GM, where is the raffle? Yellow GM, may I borrow tape?{pause}The color system works so well that nobody says a name anymore.{pause}GM A points out that his scarf is red, but his favorite color is blue.{pause}GM D admits the umbrella handle squeaks directly beside his audio cable.{pause}They trade two items for comfort, then forget to update the schedule.{pause}The first successful system begins drifting almost immediately.

nodes.name: Gm A3
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Garden requests Green, but Green is now holding Blue at the stage.{pause}Yellow borrowed Red's scarf because the supply room was cold.{pause}Red carries the green bag after delivering tape to the flowers.{pause}Every accessory is useful, which means every accessory keeps moving.{pause}The GMs begin announcing both color and station on each radio call.{pause}Guests follow the voices and stop trusting what they see.

nodes.name: Gm A4
nodes.speaker: GM B
nodes.dialogue: New rule: colors identify the task, not the person.{pause}Whoever carries the green bag becomes garden support for that trip.{pause}The red scarf marks welcome duty, even when worn over one elbow.{pause}The blue umbrella marks stage weather and emergency cable shade.{pause}The GMs trade roles smoothly while keeping favorite jobs in rotation.{pause}Accessories fail as names but succeed as a moving work plan.

nodes.name: Gm B1
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Fine. Be one volunteer in four places through a perfect relay.{pause}Welcome GM greets a guest, then radios the request ahead.{pause}Supply GM prepares the item before the guest reaches the next room.{pause}Garden GM guides the route while Stage GM completes the final task.{pause}Each handoff begins with SAME GM, NEXT STATION and one bell chime.{pause}The event gains a single helper who seems to teleport politely.

nodes.name: Gm B2
nodes.speaker: Guest
nodes.dialogue: GM found my lost hat at the door, then handed it to me on stage.{pause}GM also loaned me tape while explaining the rose garden.{pause}The guest assumes one astonishingly fast robot did all four jobs.{pause}GM C wants to explain, but the next relay call arrives at once.{pause}GM D completes the request and bows with the same angle as GM A.{pause}The shared performance is efficient and a little too convincing.

nodes.name: Gm B3
nodes.speaker: GM C
nodes.dialogue: Relay message: guest needs a map, a pencil, and courage for karaoke.{pause}GM A offers directions. GM B selects a pencil with a good eraser.{pause}GM C walks the guest through the quiet garden to practice breathing.{pause}GM D lowers the microphone and waits without rushing the song.{pause}One request becomes four acts of care hidden under one short name.{pause}The guest sings, then thanks GM without knowing which one to face.

nodes.name: Gm B4
nodes.speaker: GM D
nodes.dialogue: The relay works, but I would like credit for the microphone part.{pause}GM B wants credit for the pencil. GM C wants credit for the walk.{pause}GM A suggests ending every relay with the names of each station.{pause}They begin saying GM at Welcome, GM at Supply, GM at Garden, GM at Stage.{pause}Guests learn that the miracle helper is really a practiced team.{pause}The shared identity becomes a story instead of a disguise.

nodes.name: Gm 11
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The main tune returns as the event reaches its busiest hour.{pause}Colored tasks and relay habits survive in the same new routine.{pause}A radio call goes to a station, then to the GM who enjoys it most.{pause}Guests begin using role names when they remember them.{pause}When they do not, all four still answer the simple call for GM.{pause}The identity crisis has become a flexible volunteer network.

nodes.name: Gm 12
nodes.speaker: Photographer
nodes.dialogue: Group photo in fifteen minutes. I need every volunteer's full name.{pause}The coordinator checks the original form and finds four entries: GM.{pause}The photographer also wants one caption describing each person's role.{pause}GM A has worked welcome, garden, supply, and stage by now.{pause}Every accessory has moved, and every relay included all four.{pause}The photograph demands fixed identities after a day of useful swapping.

nodes.name: Gm 13
nodes.speaker: GM A
nodes.dialogue: Maybe the caption can describe what each of us noticed today.{pause}GM B noticed empty supply bins before anybody had to ask.{pause}GM C noticed guests who needed quiet before joining the crowd.{pause}GM D noticed every cable people were about to trip over.{pause}GM A noticed who entered alone and made sure they had directions.{pause}Those differences feel more real than letters assigned at breakfast.{pause}They test the idea by covering their letter badges and asking volunteers whom they would{pause}seek for four ordinary problems.{pause}Without hesitation, people point toward the supply expert, the calm greeter, the careful stagehand,{pause}and the guide who remembers every entrance.{pause}Nobody mentions armor shade or shoulder shape; they describe habits, promises, and the small{pause}moments that made the event easier.{pause}GM D writes each answer beneath the unfinished caption, leaving enough space for the others to{pause}revise his wording.

nodes.name: Gm 14
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: The Volunteer of the Day ballot creates another problem.{pause}Every nomination says GM because every station used the same name.{pause}One note praises the garden walk. One praises a perfectly chosen pencil.{pause}Another thanks the stage helper, and six thank the welcome desk.{pause}The ballots recognize four people while naming only one.{pause}All four GMs laugh until the coordinator realizes this is serious.

nodes.name: Gm 15
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Photo setup ready. Four floor marks form a neat straight line.{pause}The red scarf, yellow cap, green bag, and blue umbrella await assignment.{pause}The photographer can capture four distinct role portraits.{pause}Or the GMs can keep matching badges and share one team caption.{pause}The choice will decide how tomorrow's volunteers remember today.{pause}It will also decide who receives the single gold certificate.

nodes.name: Gm 16
nodes.speaker: GM C
nodes.dialogue: I do not need a different face. I need my work to be visible.{pause}GM D says being seen together should not erase being seen separately.{pause}GM B holds the four ballots beneath the returning title melody.{pause}GM A straightens every identical badge with quiet care.{pause}They can invent personal role titles or embrace the shared GM name.{pause}Either answer must make room for four voices, not one replacement.{pause}They pass the ballots around once more and add a rule: no title may describe only what armor{pause}looks like.{pause}Each name must help a stranger know whom they are addressing and remind the wearer what care they{pause}promised to provide.{pause}The coordinator offers to print anything they choose, including four copies of the same answer{pause}if that answer is deliberate.{pause}For the first time all day, sameness becomes an option instead of an assumption.

nodes.name: Gm 17
nodes.speaker: Photographer
nodes.dialogue: Positions, please. Tell me exactly what goes under the picture.{pause}The accessories sit in a box after changing hands all afternoon.{pause}The radios rest together, still blinking with old station calls.{pause}Guests gather behind the camera and begin chanting GM, GM, GM.{pause}The four volunteers look at one another and count down together.{pause}This final choice will turn a confusing badge into a public answer.

nodes.name: Gm C1
nodes.speaker: GM A
nodes.dialogue: Welcome GM, Supply GM, Garden GM, and Stage GM.{pause}They choose the titles by favorite moments, not current accessories.{pause}Welcome GM wears the blue umbrella because rain starts again.{pause}Supply GM keeps the red scarf warm around both shoulders.{pause}Garden GM carries the yellow cap, while Stage GM holds the green bag.{pause}The mismatched colors prove the roles belong to people, not props.

nodes.name: Gm C2
nodes.speaker: Photographer
nodes.dialogue: Now trade one accessory to the person who helped you most.{pause}The instruction causes a cheerful storm of scarves, bags, and umbrellas.{pause}Every GM helped every other GM, so every item moves more than once.{pause}The camera catches them laughing before anybody becomes organized.{pause}That unplanned picture shows four identical robots making four faces.{pause}The photographer declares it the only honest portrait of the day.

nodes.name: Gm C3
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Volunteer awards go to four roles performed by four people.{pause}The gold certificate is cut into four careful equal panels.{pause}Each panel lists one role and one detail from a grateful ballot.{pause}Together the pieces spell GM across the bottom edge.{pause}The accessory-exchange tune plays while the team fits them together.{pause}Nothing was divided until everyone could still read the whole award.

nodes.name: Gm C4
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Next year, badges include a blank line for favorite volunteer role.{pause}The four GMs still arrive together and still answer the same radio call.{pause}Guests learn their titles, preferences, and matching umbrella squeaks.{pause}Accessories continue changing hands whenever a task changes.{pause}The group photo hangs at the entrance beneath four role captions.{pause}In the corner, all four have written the same proud name: GM.

nodes.name: Gm D1
nodes.speaker: GM D
nodes.dialogue: Keep the shared name. Everyone answers, and everyone speaks.{pause}The four GMs stand shoulder to shoulder with identical badges visible.{pause}No accessory marks rank, role, or permanent assignment.{pause}The photographer asks who ran welcome, and four hands rise.{pause}He asks who worked stage, garden, and supply. Four hands rise again.{pause}The photo captures one name supported by sixteen completed shifts.

nodes.name: Gm D2
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Volunteer of the Day is GM. All four bow at the same moment.{pause}Then each steps forward to read one of the grateful ballots aloud.{pause}Garden, pencil, stage, and welcome stories receive equal applause.{pause}The single certificate is signed by every guest who remembers a moment.{pause}Its border fills with tiny names around the large printed GM.{pause}A shared title becomes a place where individual thanks can collect.

nodes.name: Gm D3
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: When cleanup radio calls GM, all four answer one last time.{pause}They fold tables, gather pencils, guide guests, and coil stage cables.{pause}Nobody wastes time deciding which GM the message intended.{pause}The everyone-answers tune turns the work into a four-part rhythm.{pause}At the door, the coordinator finally finds the lost A-B-C-D notepad.{pause}She recycles it without asking whether anyone wants the letters.

nodes.name: Gm D4
nodes.speaker: GM A
nodes.dialogue: The name was never the problem. The silence after it was.{pause}Now any call for GM receives four answers with four useful ideas.{pause}Their badges remain identical, but their introductions become longer.{pause}I am GM, welcome specialist. I am GM, keeper of good pencils.{pause}I am GM, garden guide. I am GM, protector of stage cables.{pause}Four GMs leave beneath one umbrella rhythm and four separate waves.
